item.content:encoded:
A new proof that SCP, it wasn't better at the old days. Seriously, I realize that just now, this article straight-up looks like the jokes about bad relationships that I was reading on old joke compilation books when I was a kid. This type of jokes when the woman is depicted as an incarnation of the Devil and the man is depicted as a jerk who is too lazy to try to live a more healthy relationship and too idiot to realize that divorce exist, instead of the more dubious means he can often use for ending his relationship.

And that -J is just that. A joke from a shitty joke compilation book with just a little SCP flavour on top of that and that's all. No subversion of the thing, no twist, just an unfunny, annoying "joke" for boomers. Nothing redeeming about it.

-1, would downvote more if I could.

Putting aside the misogynistic/offensive overtones (personally I didn't feel that way so much, but it's not hard to comprehend why others have said as much)..

The prose itself seems quite rough/unrefined. Like; I think the tone isn't proper-clinical as it should be for a SCP document, but isn't 'off' enough for it to be like a format screw (e.g. written by a non-researcher member of staff (and it says it's written by an Overseer, so even then it wouldn't be fitting)). Furthermore, what potential humour there could be in this idea doesn't come out thorough this execution.

So, those are the opinions of mine that guided my vote.

item.title: Re: Joke
item.content:encoded:
It's an unfunny joke. It's less amusing than what the US pays teachers and soldiers, which is a particularly unfunny joke in its own right.

In addition, claiming that something offensive is "just a joke" only serves to marginalize those taking legitimate offense to the subject matter.

I, for one, came away offended and not amused. I accordingly award this article one negative point.

EDIT: Oh, and I would be equally offended if the subject were male. It's like my offense level at a campaign sign being within the "no electioneering" radius of a polling place - I'm equally offended whether I support the candidate or not.
